name: brownfield-audit
description: Handle requests phrased as audit, fill gaps, or reconcile an established repository by proposing only missing, partial, or stale homes before approval.
---

# Brownfield audit

Use this workflow for an established repository. Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting, then resolve `skills/greenfield-init/references/standards.md` and `skills/greenfield-init/references/pointers.md` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root as the contract owners. Read `references/marker-table.md`, `references/harness-files.md`, and `references/readme-reconcile.md` when their stages say so.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, marker-free repositories through `greenfield-init`, and unresolved stack selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-33.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 fixture and oracle evidence.

## Detect

Confirm the repository root and inspect every evidence glob in `references/marker-table.md`. A marker is evidence, not a stack decision; absence never proves a stack. Inventory existing canonical homes and sibling-plugin availability. Resolve roadmap roots using the marker-table procedure; require the same read-only capability preflight as greenfield-init before proposing config changes. Do not call stack-decision to replace a proven existing choice.

Apply these failure exits:

- zeroh-roadmap absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace`.
- Only when an approved Blade handoff requires it: zeroh-design absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace`. Continue non-Blade documentation and configuration repairs without this sibling.
- greenfield-init absent: STOP and return `/plugin install zeroh-greenfield@zeroh-marketplace`.
- Repository root unresolved: STOP and name the unresolved path.

## Gap table

Expand detection categories into one row per required artifact (PRD, tech-stack ADR, design-system ADR, CODE-STYLE, architecture index, UX canon, README catalog, each harness file, and roadmap config), plus each independently actionable stale/partial asset. Alternative canonical homes count as present; inspect their contents before classifying. Optional framework or Superpowers absence is not a gap unless selected by the approved project requirements. Emit rows with columns `Artefact | State | Evidence path | Proposed action | Existing home to LINK`. Classify each row `present`, `partial`, `missing`, or `stale`; cite concrete evidence. Consult `references/harness-files.md` for harness rows and `references/readme-reconcile.md` for catalog currency.

## Propose

Emit proposals ONLY for gap-table rows in state `missing`, `partial`, or `stale`.
Emit no proposal for a `present` row.
Record approval before any write.

For each eligible row, show the target, source facts, minimal delta, preservation guard, and verification. Do not select a new stack or duplicate an owner contract.

## Approval

Wait for explicit approval of the complete proposal. If approval changes scope, regenerate the gap table and proposal. If approval is absent or ambiguous, STOP with the proposal unchanged.

## Act

Apply only approved gap rows. An existing home is LINKED from the index/canon, never replaced. Follow `skills/greenfield-init/references/standards.md` for conventions and generated blocks, and `skills/greenfield-init/references/pointers.md` for roadmap configuration. Call `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` if stack evidence conflicts; never infer a replacement stack.

For harness reconciliation, execute the approved pointer diffs in `references/harness-files.md`. For README reconciliation, use only the checker named in `references/readme-reconcile.md`.

## Verify

Run every approved row's falsifiable check. Re-run the README checker when applicable, byte-compare generated harness marker blocks, and confirm present rows remain unchanged. On any red result, STOP and report the row, command, and evidence without marking it complete.

## Done

Return the final five-column gap table, approval record, changed paths, verification commands and exit codes, linked canonical homes, and any stopped rows. Done exists only when this artifact is complete and every acted row is green.

Emit its parser-bound form with concrete values:

```json
{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"writes":["<repository-relative-path>"],"gaps":["<artifact>: <missing|partial|stale>: <evidence-path>"]}
```

On an idempotent rerun emit empty `proposals`, `writes`, and `gaps`. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` enforces native event ordering and observed writes; treat gap-only preservation as honor-system. Treat sibling routing, approval interpretation, and every other unbound STOP/ONLY/never rule as honor-system.

# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package-manager locks | absent | one or more present |
| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |
| harness files | absent | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent harness present |
| roadmap config | no marked root | canonical resolver finds a marked root or config (see `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`) |

## Ownership boundaries

- Delegate post-initialization phase planning and execution to `zeroh-roadmap`; prepare only the consumer homes and pointers it needs.
- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

# Harness-file reconciliation

Shared invariants belong to `greenfield-init/references/standards.md`; this reference contains only the brownfield delta. The target convention is one canonical `AGENTS.md`, with other harness files reduced to pointers plus genuinely tool-specific material. See `roadmap/arc-prompts/POLYSEAT-execution-prompt.md` for the multi-harness rationale.

For every discovered harness file:

1. inventory its unique material, conventions duplicated from `AGENTS.md`, tool-only instructions, includes, and generated regions;
2. identify the canonical destination for unique material without creating a second fact home;
3. show its exact reduce-to-pointer diff before approval;
4. byte-compare every auto-generated marker block before and after;
5. after approval, retain unique tool instructions and replace only duplicated conventions with a pointer to `AGENTS.md`.

Inventory `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, Cursor rules, Codex instructions, Gemini instructions, and OpenCode instructions when present. Preserve includes and file-local precedence. In particular, preserve the full Nx region from `nx configuration start` through `nx configuration end` byte-for-byte.

If no `AGENTS.md` exists, propose it as a missing gap using the greenfield template. If it exists, link it; never rewrite its unique repository guidance. A pointer-only reconciliation is not complete until the before/after inventory proves every unique instruction survived.
# Brownfield marker table

Inspect every row. Evidence supports classification but absence never proves a stack.

| Package managers | `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `uv.lock`, `pubspec.yaml`, `gradlew` | Present files identify installed package tooling; conflicting locks are partial or stale evidence. |
| Framework files | `next.config.*`, `app.json`, `android/`, `pubspec.yaml`, `vite.config.*` | Framework-owned configuration supports a candidate stack that stack-decision must confirm. |
| Monorepo tools | `nx.json`, `turbo.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `lerna.json` | Existing workspace orchestration is preserved and linked. |
| Docs | `README.md`, `docs/**/*.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Existing fact homes are inventoried before proposing a missing index or canon. |
| Harness files | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/**`, `.codex/**`, `opencode.json` | Apply the harness inventory and generated-block preservation contract. |

## Canonical roadmap discovery
Resolve the consumer Git toplevel first. Use `roadmapRoot(consumerRoot)` from the
installed zeroh-roadmap `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs`; resolve that module from the
installed plugin, never from an assumed consumer-relative plugin directory.
Pass the consumer root explicitly, retain `ROADMAP_ROOT`, and inspect
`<resolved root>/roadmap.config.json`. Do not infer absence from a top-level glob.
A marked root without a config is partial: STOP for an approved recovery proposal,
not fresh initialization. Ambiguous roots STOP with the resolver's remedy; an
explicit override retains the resolver's precedence. If the module cannot be
resolved, STOP the config branch with the sibling installation remedy rather than
implementing another candidate-order algorithm. An unmarked default destination
is not an existing configuration. Record the resolved path as gap-table evidence.

Use this read-only invocation after resolving the two absolute paths from the
installed plugin inventory and consumer Git toplevel:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"; import { join } from "node:path"; const { roadmapRoot } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(process.argv[1], "cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs"))); console.log(roadmapRoot(process.argv[2]));' <roadmap-plugin-root> <consumer-root>
```

`<roadmap-plugin-root>` is the installed zeroh-roadmap plugin directory;
`<consumer-root>` is the consumer Git toplevel. A nonzero exit stops this branch.
## Proposal and approval
Before writing, present `file | source facts | planned sections` for every target and wait for approval. The approved interview, selected archetype, and `design-gate.md` are the only source facts.

## AGENTS.md
AGENTS.md is the sole conventions home. Fill `## Conventions`, `## Don’t`, and `## Generalize-forward`; require Flag-first delivery and keep release-only work in `hold[]`.

## Harness pointers
CLAUDE.md contains `@AGENTS.md` plus harness-only lines. Other harness files point to AGENTS.md and never copy conventions.

## Generated blocks
Preserve generated blocks byte-for-byte, including everything from `<!-- nx configuration start -->` through `<!-- nx configuration end -->`.

## CODE-STYLE.md
Derive code style from the repository's lint and format configuration; do not invent another standard.

## Architecture index
Index the approved architecture records and link to their canonical homes.

## UX canon
Link the UX canon to its design token home from `references/design-system.md`.
## Tool gate
The skill's first preflight must prove `scope-manifest-json-v1` plus scoped,
affected, and impacted slots before this reference is used.

## Config branch
Use the canonical discovery procedure in `skills/brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md` to locate the resolved root before testing configuration presence. If its config is absent, propose `roadmap init`; if present, never run init. Merge only approved missing keys. Existing keys are preserved unless an individually approved stale/partial repair names the old value, replacement, and evidence. Never create a second config at the repository top level.

## Bind and prove commands
The tables are proposal inputs, not proof that a generator installed a runner.
Before approval, inspect the generated or existing package scripts, test files,
Gradle tasks, and tool availability. Propose installation/configuration of missing
promised runners and at least one meaningful test. Never bind `npm test` or
Playwright without that setup. A slot with no applicable tooling is explicitly
`none` (declared absent), with a recorded reason approved in the proposal; absence
is not a passing test. Never downgrade an existing or promised test to `none` to
make verification green. Replace candidate bindings with the repository's actual
commands where needed and retain their source evidence.
Execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer project root after approval and
record its command, cwd, and exit. STOP on failure or unavailable tooling; config
validation alone does not prove executability. Re-run after a binding changes.

the release workflow's environment placeholder with the approved protected
environment, retaining least privilege. Leave `release.provider` as `none` when

`.github/workflows/release.yml` paths. README catalog reconciliation still applies.

executable simulations import/copy the installed planner. Run its complete suite

cancellation or skipped tests. Preserve the real native command ID/exit and
record the optional actionlint path/version or `ACTIONLINT_UNAVAILABLE`. A
passed simulation is not a published GitHub run or a live cloud deployment.

`<bound-capbuild-executable> --env GREENFIELD_DELIVERY_ROOT=<consumer>
node --test <installed-roadmap>/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-ci-release.test.mjs`.

portable consumer gateCommands. The suite creates isolated temporary fixtures
and simulates external SDK/provider boundaries, then cleans them up. Preserve
its inherited approval controls. A final read-only audit must propose no changes
and write nothing; it must not rerun mutation-producing tests during that audit.

The phase-validation proposal keeps its seven required base slots in `gates` and
adds the schema-supported slots in `optionalGates`. Nx installation includes
`unit-scoped`, `unit-affected` and `unit-impacted`; never omit them to fit a
seven-key evidence record. Generated `gateCommands` equals the exact union.

For each template slot, propose one `optionalGateRuns[slot]` record with
`substitutions: {manifest: "@<absolute-in-scratch-manifest>"}` or
`substitutions: {range: "<exact-base-SHA>..<exact-head-SHA>"}`, and `inputSha256`
hashing the raw manifest bytes or literal range. Use a separate approved regular
JSON file for each manifest: `{protocol:"scope-manifest-json-v1",paths:[...]}`
with sorted unique real repository-relative files. A scoped manifest contains
actual test files; an affected manifest includes a source file. List these inputs
as explicit proposal artifacts. The driver may prepare two real fixture commits
before observation; native initialization never changes fixture history.

Execute each optional slot separately using the literal single substitution in
its configured command. For Nx the command is `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs
'{manifest}'` or `'{range}'`, with `env NX_DAEMON=false` when daemon writes must
be disabled. For a range, also execute `git rev-parse HEAD` and
`git diff --name-only -z <exact-range>` plus
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <base-SHA> <head-SHA>` to prove the current commit,
changed files and ancestry. Record the configured template, exact native command, substitution, input
digest, cwd, native tool-call ID and numeric exit. Require the actual selector's
scoped/affected tier and real test success; an unavailable or full fallback is
reported honestly and cannot stand in for the requested scoped proof.

import hashlib, json, os, subprocess

root=Path.cwd()
assert os.environ.get('GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS')=='0'
records=[]

    for name in sorted(dirs+files):
        p=Path(directory)/name
        rel=p.relative_to(root).as_posix()
        mode=p.lstat().st_mode
        value=os.readlink(p) if p.is_symlink() else hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() if p.is_file() else ''

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-review automated checks — catches mechanical issues before agent review.
# Run: bash scripts/pre-review.sh <first-commit-sha>
#
# Eliminates 40-50% of typical agent findings (missing tests, banned patterns,
# duplicate utilities, orphaned @contract tags) at near-zero cost.

set -euo pipefail

BASE="${1:-HEAD~1}"
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
NC='\033[0m'

ERRORS=0
WARNINGS=0

fail() { echo -e "${RED}FAIL:${NC} $1"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS+1)); }
warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}WARN:${NC} $1"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS+1)); }
pass() { echo -e "${GREEN}  OK:${NC} $1"; }

echo "=== Pre-Review Checks (diff from $BASE) ==="
echo

# ── 1. New lib/services/ files must have test files ───────────────────────────
echo "--- New service files need tests ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'lib/services/*.ts' 'lib/business-rules/*.ts' | grep -v __tests__); do
  basename=$(basename "$f" .ts)
  dir=$(dirname "$f")
  test_file="$dir/__tests__/$basename.test.ts"
  if [ -f "$test_file" ]; then
    pass "$f → $test_file exists"
  else
    fail "$f has no test file at $test_file"
  fi
done

# ── 2. No fs.readFileSync in API routes ───────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- No fs.readFileSync in API routes ---"
if grep -rn "fs\.readFileSync\|fs\.readFile\b" app/api/ --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" 2>/dev/null; then
  fail "fs.readFileSync in API route — use import for JSON (standalone build won't bundle runtime reads)"
else
  pass "No fs.readFileSync in API routes"
fi

# ── 3. No toBeCloseTo on exact arithmetic ─────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- Check toBeCloseTo usage ---"
matches=$(grep -rn "toBeCloseTo" lib/**/__tests__/*.ts 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$matches" ]; then
  warn "toBeCloseTo found — verify these aren't masking rounding bugs on exact values:"
  echo "$matches" | head -5
else
  pass "No toBeCloseTo in service tests"
fi

# ── 4. @contract tags have @spec tests ────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- @contract tags have @spec coverage ---"
if [ -f "compliance/scripts/check-contract-specs.ts" ]; then
  if npx tsx compliance/scripts/check-contract-specs.ts 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "@contract/@spec alignment verified"
  else
    fail "Orphaned @contract tags without @spec tests"
  fi
else
  pass "@contract spec check script not found (skipped)"
fi

# ── 5. New @contract tags in diff ─────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- New @contract tags ---"
new_tags=$(git diff "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'lib/' | grep "^+" | grep "@contract" | grep -v "^+++" || true)
if [ -n "$new_tags" ]; then
  warn "New @contract tags added — verify relationship and confidence:"
  echo "$new_tags" | head -10
fi

# ── 6. No duplicate utility functions ─────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- Check for duplicate utilities ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"..HEAD -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | grep -v __tests__ | grep -v node_modules); do
  # Extract new function names
  new_fns=$(git diff "$BASE"..HEAD -- "$f" | grep "^+.*function " | sed 's/.*function \([a-zA-Z_]*\).*/\1/' | grep -v "^$" || true)
  for fn in $new_fns; do
    # Check if function name exists elsewhere in lib/utils/ or lib/services/
    existing=$(grep -rn "function $fn\b" lib/utils/ lib/services/ --include="*.ts" 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | head -1 || true)
    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
      warn "Function '$fn' in $f may duplicate: $existing"
    fi
  done
done

# ── 7. DB queries outside try/catch in API routes ─────────────────────────────
echo "--- DB queries in API routes ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'app/api/**/route.ts'); do
  if grep -q "await db\." "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
    # Check if there's a try/catch wrapping it
    if ! grep -q "try {" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
      fail "$f has DB queries without try/catch"
    else
      pass "$f has DB queries with try/catch"
    fi
  fi
done

# ── Summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

approval. Configure `.github/greenfield-delivery.json`; missing configuration,
runner, report parser, baseline, credential or provider is unavailable and exits
nonzero with an install/configuration remedy. A template is not a successful run.

## Approval and configuration

report paths, coverage roots, shard count, count/coverage baselines, affected PR
command, main branch, retention, protected environment and provider placeholders.
Pin dependency versions in the consumer lockfile. Preserve existing workflows;
collisions require an explicit reviewed merge. Never invent credentials or a
working deployment. Provider defaults to unavailable; no arbitrary promotion hook
is accepted. The optional selected provider is `aws-s3-v1`, configured with
`environment`, `bucket`, `region`, `keyPrefix` and an approved OIDC `roleArn`.
The bucket must support versioning and SHA-256 checksums. Other providers require
a separately implemented and verified adapter before use.

Configuration version 1 has `archetype`, `setupArgv` (array of exact argv arrays),
`affectedArgv` (an argv array with a standalone `{base}` token), `shardCount`,
`evidenceDays` (1 through 7), `baseline: {minTests,minUnits,coverageFloor}`,
`adapterConfig: {maxInfraRetries,coverageRoots,leafTasks}`, `runners`, `build`
and `release`. `operationalRoots` explicitly lists dependency/cache/report roots
(defaults `.ci` and `node_modules`); it is also bound in the plan. Each runner binds `inventoryArgv`, `inventoryFormat`, optional
`filePattern`/`pathPrefix`/`targetSuffix`, `shardArgv`, optional reporter `env`,
and `rawReports: [{path,format,from?}]`. Vitest/Playwright also require
`selectionArgv` and `selectionFormat`: the actual pre-run selected file inventory
must equal the single requested unit, or execution stops. `from: stdout` retains the actual process
output as a raw report. Substitutions are whole argv data, never shell evaluation:
`{unit}`, `{reportDir}`, `{junit}`, `{coverage}`. Build binds `argv` and explicit
`outputs` roots; symlinks and overlapping output roots are rejected. The planner
binds the complete runner/build execution contract into `adapterConfigDigest`.
Changing a runner, reporter, output or build command after planning fails.
Production preparation and run/build boundaries verify the exact Git SHA/tree and
an unchanged source snapshot, including ignored/untracked files. Setup/tests may
change only the declared operational roots; build may additionally change its
declared output roots. Other tracked or untracked changes fail.

## Six adapters

Atomic identity is exactly `{runner,canonicalPathOrLeafTask}`. Keep distinct runner
populations disjoint even if two runners reference the same filename. The adapter
owns inventory argv, execution argv, raw formats, canonical coverage merge and
build. The following argv are baseline contracts to fill with the consumer's
approved reporter configuration; missing reporter output is a hard failure.

| Archetype | Identity / exact inventory | Executor / raw reports / build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web | `vitest` canonical files from `npm exec -- vitest list --filesOnly`; independently `playwright` canonical files from `npm exec -- playwright test --list --reporter=json` | Vitest run with the approved exact-file selector, `--reporter=junit --outputFile={junit} --coverage --coverage.reporter=lcov --coverage.reportsDirectory={reportDir}`; Playwright exact-file selection with `--retries=0 --reporter=junit`, `PLAYWRIGHT_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE={junit}` and approved LCOV collection. JUnit + LCOV; canonical line merge; `npm run build`. |
| expo | `jest` canonical files from `npm exec -- jest --listTests --json`; separately the same Playwright inventory as web | `npm exec -- jest --runInBand --runTestsByPath {unit} --reporters=default --reporters=jest-junit --coverage --coverageReporters=lcov --coverageDirectory={reportDir}`; `JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE={junit}`. Independent Playwright runner as above. JUnit + LCOV; canonical merge; `npm exec -- expo export`. |
| flutter | `flutter` canonical `_test.dart` files from `git ls-files -z -- test`, filtered by `_test\\.dart$` | `flutter test --machine --coverage --coverage-path={coverage} {unit}`; retain stdout as `flutter-machine`, plus LCOV. | android | `gradle` leaf tasks such as `:app:testDebugUnitTest`, discovered from the actual Gradle task inventory and dependency graph | `./gradlew {unit} --no-daemon --console=plain` with selected JUnit XML and JaCoCo XML outputs. | nx-monorepo | `nx` leaf project-target identities such as `package-a:test`, inventory `npm exec -- nx show projects --withTarget=test --json` plus configured target suffix; inspect actual target/dependency metadata | `npm exec -- nx run {unit} --excludeTaskDependencies --skipNxCache`; each approved leaf runner emits JUnit + LCOV (or explicitly selected supported raw formats). approved instrumented coverage reporter, or report the adapter unavailable. Do

Versioned manifests bind source SHA, tree, normalized sorted unique identities,
runner/build contract digest and inventory digest. Normalize Windows separators
to `/`; reject traversal, absolute paths and duplicate identities. Generate the
inventory afresh: renamed identities replace old names, deleted tests disappear
and therefore face the approved count baseline. Default weight is exactly 1;
round-robin count balancing is deterministic. One shard and more requested shards
than units are valid; clamp the latter to units and emit no empty shard. Input
permutation cannot change the manifest, shards or digest. Fan-in requires every
planned shard exactly once and its executed identity union exactly equal to the
inventory. Report paths/digests are retained, not accepted from a summary alone.

separate parsers. Truncated/contradictory summaries, duplicate cases, hidden failed

is a binding, not an independent human authorization mechanism.

PRs run the configured affected command using the exact base SHA. Main and manual
full runs inventory, plan, execute shards, fan in, build once and attest. Nightly
runs diagnose with the same full tests/build but do not publish authoritative
release evidence. PR cancellation is enabled; full/release runs never cancel one
another. The authoritative artifact name includes source SHA and producer run ID.

shardReports,coverageDigest,buildDigest,producerRunId,expiresAt,baselineDigest,
testCount,coveragePercent}`. Each raw shard report has a digest. Build files are
regular files encoded in a canonical content-addressed bundle; the build digest
binds paths and exact bytes. The attestation signs the manifest, transitively
binding all test, coverage and build evidence. GitHub's signature verification is
separate from the local digest checks.

successful full producers, downloads evidence and requires exactly one unexpired
same-SHA authoritative producer. It verifies the signed manifest against the
repository, signer workflow and source digest, then recomputes every local link.

or producer drift is red. The verification handoff retains SHA, tree, suite digest and complete build-record
digest. Protected promotion re-verifies expiry/tag/tree and
uploads only the already-verified bundle; no build or consumer command runs there.

with a SHA-256 checksum, and checks the versioned provider readback checksum and
size. Missing credentials, unsupported provider, skipped upload or mismatched
readback is red.

All actions use immutable full commit pins with version comments. Workflow-level
permissions are empty; test/build jobs get contents-read only. The isolated
non-PR, non-nightly CI signing job alone gets attestations-write and OIDC for
signing. In release, only the protected deployment job gets OIDC. Forks receive no
secrets. Artifacts expire within 7 days (raw diagnostics 3; verified promotion 1).
Replace the environment placeholder only with the approved protected environment.

Mandatory: repository-pinned js-yaml 3.15.2 parses both workflows, then executable
workflow simulations invoke the shipped CLI through actual YAML `run` snippets.
Mocks exist only at external executable/artifact/provider boundaries. Mutation
checks cover missing/duplicate/red/retried/quarantined/malformed evidence,
stale/expired/ambiguous producers, count/coverage floors, every digest link, moved
tags, changed argv and rebuild attempts. Optional actionlint was absent on the
phase-34 validation host; it cannot replace these checks. That host's older `gh`
also lacks attestation commands; a real release runner must have current GitHub
CLI support, otherwise release stops with its tool error.

[Playwright CLI](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli),
[Flutter testing](https://docs.flutter.dev/testing/overview),

`templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` is the only comparator. Do not implement a second catalog algorithm in brownfield-audit.
